question: How does the throb of consciousness appear when present in both inner and outer alike?
premises: The throb of consciousness is of the nature of three powers.
It possesses both contraction and expansion.
This holds even in the pair of inner and outer, appearing as beautiful in both common and other forms.
inference: The throb of consciousness, possessing contraction and expansion and made of three powers, appears beautiful in common and other forms even within inner and outer.
uncertainties: The distinction between common and other forms is experiential rather than fixed.
plain_english: Even in the inner and outer pair, the throb of consciousness, made of three powers and possessing contraction and expansion, appears beautiful in both common and other forms.
